observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a dark brown, mottled, many-legged creature seen from the front. It has a broad flat carapace with knobbly edges, two small eyes, a cluster of fang-like mouthparts hanging down and about eight curved, segmented legs splayed out. A thick stalk rises from the top of the carapace and curls over to hold a glossy gold orb. East: a long, low side profile. The back is spiky and finned, the head points right with a small eye and a fringe of long downward fangs, the legs are curved and spread, and the stalk rises from just behind the head and curls forward to the gold orb. North: the same creature from behind. A ridged, segmented, wedge-shaped back tapers toward the camera, and about six curved legs splay to the sides. The stalk comes up from the far (head) end and holds the gold orb above the body. No eyes or mouth are visible. The north body is slightly narrower than the south body.
